item.title: Issue #2913 created
item.description:
Analysis and design of restricted integer types for functions.

A ranged value is a restriction on an xs:integer type where the allowed values can be defined as a RangeExpr with one of the following forms:

  • A to B -- for the range A <= x <= B for any value x in the type (i.e. with a restricted upper and lower bound);
  • () to B for the range x <= B for any value x in the type (i.e. with an unrestricted lower bound and a restricted upper bound);
  • A to () for the range |A <= x for any value x in the type (i.e. with a restricted lower bound and an unrestricted upper bound);
  • () to () -- for any value x in the type (i.e. with an unrestricted upper and lower bound).

For predefined types this gives for example:

  • xs:integer = () to ()
  • xs:nonNegativeInteger = 0 to ()
  • xs:positiveInteger = 1 to ()
  • xs:negativeInteger = () to -1
  • xs:short = -32_768 to 32_767

Possible syntax example:

let $x as xs:integer in range 1 to 10 := 4;

i.e. it is an extension of a TypeDeclaration.

Note: This could be extended to the other xs:numeric types as ranges are not just limited to xs:integer values.

Note: A processor could use this information to generate something along the lines of "value is not an instance of xs:long in the range 2 to 20" which would be more helpful to the user.

Note: This should cover most use cases. The only missing case is a unicode codepoint type which is outside the scope of this proposal.
